reason: Yomitan replaces the text with its letters alone. wty-yi-en, the recommended dictionary, writes 43,497 of its 58,213 headwords with points (YIVO spelling), so pointed text no longer reaches them: with Yomitan's four processors the pack's rules reach 36.9% of the corpus sample instead of 97.4%, first rank 34.0% instead of 90.7% (README.md, Measurements). The pack keeps the text as written and adds points where unpointed text leaves them out (addPoints).

Yomitan writes the first וו, וי, יי, יִ, ייַ, אַ and אָ of a text as one character (װ, ױ, ײ and the presentation forms). wty-yi-en writes them as two letters (19,663 headwords with וו, 44 with װ; no presentation forms), so the combined text matches nothing until convertYiddishLigatures splits it again. The pack splits ligatures instead (splitLigatures) and keeps ײַ, which wty-yi-en uses for ay.

Yomitan's rules leave a stem's last letter medial (קויפֿנ, מאנ) and this postprocessor writes it final. The pack's rules write the final letter themselves (מאַכט → מאַכן, וואָכן → וואָך), and Yomitan's rules are not in transforms.json (README.md, Rule provenance), so the pack has no postprocessor.

Undoes combineYiddishLigatures for the query (it returns the text, its first ligatures split and its first letter pairs combined). The pack never combines letters, and the combined variant matches no wty-yi-en headword.
